name: Peacock Peperomia
description: Peperomia albovittata is a compact evergreen species in the Piperaceae family, endemic to Andean montane cloud forests in Ecuador, where it grows as a terrestrial or epiphytic herb. It is known for deeply veined foliage in green, silver, and purple-brown tones with pinkish-red stems. The semi-succulent leaves store water, so the plant prefers bright indirect light and should be watered only after the top of the mix has dried. Average indoor humidity and warm temperatures (about 18–24 °C) suit it well. Tiny flower spikes may appear in spring. Non-toxic to pets and humans. Popular cultivars include 'Piccolo Banda' and others selected for especially bold leaf patterning. Wild populations are geographically restricted and conservation-sensitive.
careTips: Provide bright indirect light; avoid harsh direct sun which can scorch the leaves
Allow the top 1–2 cm of soil to dry between waterings; better to underwater than overwater
Use a well-draining, airy mix with perlite or bark
Average room humidity (40–60%) is usually enough; higher humidity is beneficial
Keep temperatures about 18–24 °C; protect from cold drafts below about 15 °C
Fertilize lightly every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer
Propagate from stem or leaf cuttings
Watch for mealybugs; non-toxic and pet-safe
geographicOrigin: Endemic to Ecuador (Andean montane cloud forests)
